A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SliM-LLM. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original perplexity and zero-shot evaluations, component and group-size ablations, GPU deployment measurements, and dialogue examples.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds allocation comparisons, further model evaluations, MMLU/MathQA results, and vision-language experiments.

M1.justification: The SBA search, GPTQ integration, and OmniQuant extension remain. However, v2 Equation 5 scales both the quantizer scale and zero point by tau, while Algorithm 2 retains v1's range-scaling and zero-point calculation. This inconsistency prevents determining whether SQC actually changed or was restated incorrectly.

E1.justification: v2 adds MMLU and MathQA evaluations and extends evaluation to LLaVA-Next-8B on AI2D, ChartQA, DocVQA, and MMBench. These substantially broaden task and modality coverage beyond v1's language-model perplexity, commonsense benchmarks, and dialogue examples.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 adds an evaluated ILP allocation comparator against SBA on four LLaMA sizes. Table 4 reports 2-bit LLaMA-7B perplexity of 17.55 for ILP versus 14.58 for SBA. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds 4-bit evaluation, Gemma2-9B and Mixtral 8x7B configurations, and LLaMA-2-70B deployment measurements; the LLaMA-2-7B deployment columns disappear. It also introduces controlled allocation and objective comparisons. The existing 128-sample, 2048-token calibration setup, default group size, and A800 hardware remain.

E4.justification: Two substantive checks of SBA's design are added: comparison with ILP allocation in Section 4.2/Table 4, and MSE versus KL-divergence objectives in Appendix D/Table 6. These test alternatives to the central allocation strategy and objective. Existing component, group-size, local-error, and salience analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty estimates. The added experiments continue reporting individual point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds results in Tables 4, 6, and 11–15, including new reasoning, multimodal, allocation, and deployment comparisons. The original perplexity, zero-shot, and group-size tables remain numerically unchanged. Deployment reporting removes LLaMA-2-7B entries and changes GPTQ's reported 2-bit runtime memory from 4.1G to 4.4G for LLaMA-7B and 7.5G to 7.6G for LLaMA-13B.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its appendix proof replace an isolated token/channel outlier argument using xx-transpose with an outlier-channel assumption using x-transpose-x and channel energy. The main Hessian definition changes accordingly, and Equation 3 becomes approximate. This substantially revises the central mathematical justification rather than merely changing notation.

C1.justification: The central SBA/SQC contributions and low-bit accuracy-efficiency claims remain. v2's introduction explicitly broadens the compatibility claim to quantization-aware training, fine-tuning-based compression, and codebook methods, beyond the demonstrated GPTQ and OmniQuant integrations emphasized in v1.

C2.justification: v2 revises the main salience explanation from clustered outlier tokens to outlier channels and describes KL allocation as aligning activation distributions rather than maximizing weight mutual information. It adds interpretations of the ILP and objective comparisons. The hardware-support limitations remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly specifies applying softmax before computing output KL divergence, and Section 3.3.2 explicitly writes the masking threshold. v1's reproducibility paragraph about supplementary scripts and dataset instructions is removed. The public code link, detailed algorithms, and mixed-precision storage implementation remain.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a dedicated mixed-precision discussion positioning group-wise allocation against HAWQ-family and OMPQ approaches. New discussion of QLoRA, LQ-LoRA, and ApiQ expands the relationship to fine-tuning methods. This substantially develops the positioning beyond v1's broader PTQ survey and criticism of fine-tuning overhead and overfitting.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, several method explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Related work gains a separate mixed-precision discussion, Algorithm 1 moves into the appendix, and broader impacts move from Appendix A to the main document. These changes substantially revise the narrative and organization.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column proceedings paper, with extensive resizing and relocation of existing displays. Seven tables are added, the deployment table loses a model column, and Figure 4's presentation changes. Most existing figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: Broader task coverage, the ILP comparison, and the revised channel-wise Hessian argument improve validation and explanation. However, the revised SQC equation conflicts with retained pseudocode, and Table 6 labels OPT-6.7B's KL perplexity as 11.27 at 2 bits while Table 8 reports 14.41, without explaining different settings. Table 14 also introduces an unexplained 23.5G/4.4G memory entry. These problems affect central method documentation and new evidence, preventing a reliable judgment of the net quality improvement.
